name: 85. Bedrock compaction routes Claude to InvokeModel (#6825)
description: Regression for #6825: a compact_20260112 edit on a bedrock/<claude> model was accepted, the compact-2026-01-12 header forwarded, and nothing compacted, because the Bedrock provider sent every Claude request through the Converse API, which AWS documents as unable to run compaction ("Compaction is currently not supported by the Converse API, however it is supported with InvokeModel", https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/claude-messages-compaction.html). Bifrost now routes such requests to InvokeModel / InvokeModelWithResponseStream with the native Anthropic Messages body. These cases stay under the 50k-token compaction trigger (cheap) and pin the egress through the response shape: usage.iterations is only ever returned by the native Anthropic body, never by Converse, and the streaming case asserts it inside the message_delta frame. Gateway 5xx fails these cases rather than skipping, since a mis-routed InvokeModel call surfaces as one; 503 and 529 are skipped only when the body names a provider capacity condition (ServiceUnavailable / overloaded_error). When the gateway has client_config.allow_per_request_raw_override enabled, x-bf-send-back-raw-request additionally exposes the outbound body and the cases assert the InvokeModel shape (anthropic_version bedrock-2023-05-31, no model field) plus the compaction edit and beta on the wire. Case 1 is the reporter's ingress (/anthropic/v1/messages, which stores context_management in ExtraParams); case 2 is its streaming variant; case 3 is the /v1/responses ingress, which stores context_management in the typed request field, so both routing inputs are covered. Folder 59 separately pins compaction billing on the Claude API.
